items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: I knew that the colored musicians... Sidney DeParis and all them guys, sharks

ctx.x: I never in my life played with a colored band on a gig. Of course, I belonged to the Clef Club and I rehearsed with them, but on an actual gig, I never in my life played with no colored band till we had the Washingtonians.

I never took it, never concentrate on it that serious, because I never come in contact with it that much, as far as playing was concerned. I knew that the colored musicians, we had just millions of them, fabulous, could play in Harlem. You could go right next door and hear the damndest horn blowing things you ever heard in your life, drummers, Big Sid Catlett, all them guys, Jabbo on trumpet, sure, Sidney DeParis and all them guys, sharks, because they had to be because it was a jungle. Everybody waiting for you…
I think Benny Goodman was the first one to present them to the public when he had Teddy and Hamp-- Lionel, in his quartet, Gene.
